title: Cart Derby: Force, Mass, and Speeding Up
subject: physical science
goal: Find out how the net force on a cart and the cart's mass change how fast it speeds up.
steps: Every cart has 10 N of friction pushing back. Net force = push − 10 N.
Rounds 1-3: the cart's mass is 20 kg. Roll for the push (table below).
Rounds 4-6: the push is 50 N. Use a mass of 10 kg, then 20 kg, then 40 kg. Before round 4, predict: does a heavier cart speed up faster or slower?
Everyone works out the net force and the acceleration (net force ÷ mass, in m/s²), and the Skeptic checks. Then the speed after 3 seconds from rest: acceleration × 3.
listen_for: A roll of 1 (a 10 N push against 10 N of friction): “it moves slowly.” Ask: what's the net force, and so what's the acceleration?
“The heavier cart goes faster because it pushes harder.” Same push, more mass: what happened to the acceleration?
Speed and acceleration mixed up: acceleration is how much the speed grows each second.
debrief: Plot acceleration against net force for rounds 1-3 on the board. What shape is it?
Ask: a cart rolls at a steady speed. What is the net force on it?
sources: The idea is also modeled in PhET Interactive Simulations' Forces and Motion: Basics (University of Colorado Boulder). The activity and questions were written for Paper Loop.
